title: Introduce dynamic telemetry tiler and contextual entropy compressor
author: Aisha Patel
description: Adds a telemetry tiler service to coalesce high-cardinality token/trace fragments into bounded tiles, a contextual entropy compressor to reduce logging cardinality while preserving anomaly signal, and a lightweight token-stitch mapper that reconstructs token-level cost/latency at invocation boundaries across services. Motivation: customer-facing incidents show noise from long-tail token/log cardinality and missing cross-service token joins, which make SLO RCAs slow and expensive. This PR implements: (1) a tiler service that groups spans/metrics by tiling keys derived from prompt shape, model variant, and tenant-decay buckets; (2) a compressor that uses frequency-based dictionarying plus contextual preservation of rare-token markers to keep anomaly fidelity; (3) an on-path token-stitch mapper that emits compact join-anchors so downstream dashboards and alerts can attribute cost/latency to end-to-end invocations. Backwards compatibility: all outputs are opt-in via a new telemetry-mode flag (off by default). Includes docs and migration notes. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] telemetry sampling knobs added - [x] runbook and alert tuning suggestions included
